title: Microsoft unveils Maia 300 AI chip
key_facts: Microsoft unveiled the Maia 300, its third-generation AI chip, on Monday (12 Oct 2026).
Microsoft says the chip is optimized for the latest reasoning AI models and agents and should lower operating costs.
Scott Guthrie, Microsoft executive vice president for cloud and AI: Microsoft expects 40% more tokens per megawatt than leading GPU-based systems.
The predecessor Maia 200 launched in January and now supports Microsoft Copilot, with GitHub Copilot and Microsoft Foundry to follow by the end of 2026.
Microsoft plans to deploy the Maia 300 after the turn of the year.
Guthrie: Azure Maia will scale to multi-gigawatt deployments from 2027, making Maia the primary inference system for Microsoft products and services.
The Verge (cited by Computerworld) notes the chip will make Microsoft less dependent on Nvidia and AMD chips.
quote_evidence: “We expect Maia 300 to deliver 40% more tokens per megawatt compared to leading GPU-based systems,” said Scott Guthrie, Microsoft’s executive vice president for cloud and AI, in a blog post.
Microsoft plans to deploy the Maia 300 after the turn of the year.
The Maia 300 will make Microsoft less dependent on AI chips from Nvidia and AMD as Microsoft shifts more workloads to its own AI chips, noted The Verge.
why_it_matters_hint: A cloud giant moving AI work onto its own chips changes the demand picture for Nvidia and AMD.
notes: Unveiled Monday 12 Oct 2026 (Microsoft Source and Yahoo Finance items are timed 12 Oct 13:00 UTC), before the 13 Oct window; Computerworld ran it 13 Oct. It does not appear in the 13 Oct pool titles, so our readers have not seen it. The 40% figure is Microsoft's own expectation.
